Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

You are an adversarial verifier. A finder claims this is LEGACY code safe to delete. Try hard to REFUTE it.

Finding: repo=andesim path=docs/MRD.md lines=46 kind=stale-doc
Claim: Product-definition table says the driver CLI 'orchestrates QEMU->vsim->QEMU handoff', describing the removed QEMU2 handback leg as a current deliverable.
Evidence given: The QEMU2 leg was removed repo-wide 2026-06-09 (docs/FRS.md:127-129 'FR-107 ... [REMOVED 2026-06-09]', CLAUDE.md:8 'there is no QEMU2 leg'). MRD is dated 2026-05-29 (pre-removal) and this row was never updated, unlike FRS.

Repo roots: andesim=/home/nick/work/andesim, vsim=/home/nick/work/vsim_andesim.
Checks you MUST do:
1. Read the file/lines yourself — does the claim match reality?
2. grep BOTH repos (tracked files) for references: filename, function names, symbols, script names, make targets, cmake targets, doc links.
3. Check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/*, Makefiles, CMake, and CLAUDE.md/docs for indirect usage (variable-built names, glob patterns like test_*.sh runners).
4. git log --follow -5 on the file: was it recently touched for a live feature?
5. Is it an INTENTIONAL fallback/compat layer per CLAUDE.md (e.g. semihost_exit.inc)?
If ANY live reference or intentional-keep reason exists, verdict isLegacy=false. Default to false when uncertain. If true, give the exact deleteScope.

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. For LLM-targeted specs (future sibling skill), use /spec-llm instead.
- csr-transport-bringup: Bring up or audit the hybrid CSR transport for an Andes RISC-V core, given the AndeStar V5 SPA PDF spec and a built vsim engine. Covers the whole pipeline: mine the spec (CSR inventory, IM Requirement / existence conditions, access modes, reset values), classify transport dispositions, bind capability gates to the engine's config.inc, and validate with the reset-hart CSR probe (--probe), the manifest completeness check, --verify, and the e2e suite. Use this skill whenever the user mentions a new core, a new vsim engine, CSR transport / transportation, CSR capability or caps gating, IM Requirement, reset value table, which mode a CSR is supported in, probe-vs-caps mismatches, exec_progbuf cmderr faults, or --verify field mismatches on Andes/M-ext CSRs -- even if they do not say "bring-up" explicitly. Also use it for engine registration work: per-engine test files, CSR manifests, completeness ("nothing missed") checks, or adding a new config of an existing core.
- deep-research: Deep research harness — fan-out web searches, fetch sources, adversarially verify claims, synthesize a cited report. - When the user wants a deep, multi-source, fact-checked research report on any topic. BEFORE invoking, check if the question is specific enough to research directly — if underspecified (e.g., "what car to buy" without budget/use-case/region), ask 2-3 clarifying questions to narrow scope. Then pass the refined question as args, weaving the answers in.
- ralph-loop:cancel-ralph: Cancel active Ralph Loop
- ralph-loop:help: Explain Ralph Loop plugin and available commands
- ralph-loop:ralph-loop: Start Ralph Loop in current session
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- verify: Verify that a code change actually does what it's supposed to by exercising it end-to-end and observing behavior — drive the affected flow, not just tests or typecheck. Run before committing nontrivial changes. Don't invoke it on a diff that only touches tests, docs, or other code with no runtime surface to drive (a change to product source always has one) — there's nothing to observe.
- code-review: Review the current diff for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud). Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).

1	# Hybrid Simulator - Market Requirements Document
2	
3	Status: draft v1.0 (commercial rewrite). Written 2026-05-29.
4	Owner: Nick. Audience: PM, BU lead, Sales engineering, Legal.
5	
6	Companion docs:
7	- `FRS.md` - functional requirements specification (engineering contract)
8	- `ROADMAP.md` - master feature roadmap (engineering plan; supersedes
9	  `docs/archive/commercial_v1_roadmap.md`)
10	- `docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb` - current ROI envelope (alpha)
11	
12	This document is the **product** view, written for a paying
13	external buyer. The previous draft (v0.1) framed hybrid_sim as an
14	Andes-internal acceleration tool. This rewrite repositions it as a
15	commercial Tier-2 EDA product competing with ARM Cycle Models,
16	Synopsys Imperas, and Wind River Simics-class hybrid offerings.
17	
18	---
19	
20	## 1. Executive Summary
21	
22	**Product name (working)**: Andes HybridSim
23	**Category**: Cycle-accurate hybrid simulator for RISC-V SoCs
24	**Cycle engine**: vsim (Verilator-derived, encrypted RTL pipeline)
25	**Fast engine**: QEMU 9.x with Andes plugin
26	**Target customer**: Andes IP licensees doing pre-silicon perf work
27	**Tier / price band**: Tier 2, $K-M/year per-seat or per-project
28	**Ship target**: Commercial v1.0 in ~12 months (engineering) +
29	6-12 months (encryption tooling) = ~18-24 months from today
30	**Differentiation**: only Tier-2 hybrid product with first-class
31	Andes IP (vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5 extensions) and zero FPGA
32	capex requirement
33	
34	**The one-line pitch**: "Cycle-exact RISC-V perf measurement on
35	real customer workloads, without an FPGA emulator or a multi-year
36	RTL learning curve."
37	
38	---
39	
40	## 2. Product Definition
41	
42	What the customer buys:
43	
44	| Component | Delivery | Purpose |
45	|---|---|---|
46	| `hsim` driver CLI | binary | orchestrates QEMU->vsim->QEMU handoff |
47	| QEMU (Andes fork) | binary + plugin SO | fast-forward engine, runs boring 99% |
48	| vsim cycle engine | **encrypted** binary | cycle-exact ROI measurement, RTL-derived but not RTL-recoverable |
49	| State transport library | linked into both | `hybrid_state_v1` wire format, mmap RAM |
50	| Trigger toolkit | linked + headers | magic-CSR, PC-watch |
51	| Pipeline trace converter | binary | kanata / Clarity DB output |
52	| Reference flow | scripts + sample workloads | bare-metal kernel, Linux userspace, SPEC-class harness |
53	| License daemon | binary | per-seat / per-project enforcement |
54	| Documentation | PDF + HTML | user guide, ABI reference, integration guide |
55	| Support | contracted | tiered SLA |
56	
57	What the customer does NOT get:
58	- Raw Verilator C++ output (encrypted only)
59	- Andes RTL or microarch internals
60	- Source of the cycle engine
61	- QEMU source (binary only; upstream QEMU available separately)
62	
63	---
64	
65	## 3. Target Market & Buyer Personas
66	
67	### 3.1 Primary buyer: Andes IP licensee SoC integrator
68	
69	| Attribute | Profile |
70	|---|---|
71	| Company size | 50-2000 engineers; cannot justify $M+ ZeBu capex |
72	| Andes IP | one or more of AX25 / AX27 / AX45 / AX46 / D23v |
73	| Workload class | OS + userspace apps, AI inference kernels, networking dataplane |
74	| Pain | QEMU is too coarse; FPGA is too late; Alioth alone is too slow on real workloads |
75	| Buying authority | Engineering VP + IT procurement; budget cycle 6-12 months |
76	| Price tolerance | $20K-200K/seat/year, $200K-2M project license |
77	
78	### 3.2 Secondary buyer: research lab / university with industry tie-in
79	
80	| Attribute | Profile |
81	|---|---|
82	| Use case | Microarchitecture research, comparative perf studies |
83	| Procurement | Grant-funded; multi-year |
84	| Price tolerance | Academic discount tier; $5K-20K/seat/year |
85	| Value to Andes | Reference publications, conference visibility, talent pipeline |
86	
87	### 3.3 Personas at the buying customer
88	
89	| Role | What they care about |
90	|---|---|
91	| **SoC Architect** | accuracy vs RTL, modeling fidelity of vendor CSRs |
92	| **Perf Engineer** | wall-clock turnaround, kanata output |
93	| **DV Engineer** | reproducibility, deterministic mode, log capture |
94	| **Engineering VP / buyer** | total cost vs FPGA capex, support SLA, lifecycle |
95	| **Legal / IP officer** | encryption guarantees, no RTL leakage, license terms |
96	| **IT / DevOps** | install footprint, license server, CI integration |
97	
98	---
99	
100	## 4. Market Sizing & Opportunity
101	
102	Rough TAM estimate (top-down):
103	
104	- Andes IP active licensees: ~300 worldwide (public Andes 2025 figures)
105	- Fraction doing serious pre-silicon perf work: ~30% = ~90 accounts
106	- Fraction with ROI-style workloads (OS + hot kernel): ~60% = ~54 accounts
107	- Realistic 3-year capture rate: 20% = ~11 paying accounts
108	- Average deal size: $100K-500K/year
109	- Year-3 ARR target: $1.1M-5.5M
110	
111	Adjacent expansion:
112	- Non-Andes RISC-V vendors (SiFive, MIPS, Tenstorrent) could license
113	  the QEMU plugin + state transport without Andes-specific vendor
114	  CSRs. Out of scope for v1.0 but TAM-meaningful.
115	- Internal Andes engineering teams (~200 engineers) consume the
116	  product at internal cost; counts as cost avoidance vs ZeBu rental.
117	
118	---
119	
120	## 5. Competitive Positioning
121	
122	### 5.1 Competitive matrix (commercial Tier 2 focus)
123	
124	| Product | Vendor | Strength | Weakness vs HybridSim | Price band |
125	|---|---|---|---|---|
126	| ARM Cycle Models + Fast Models | ARM | mature, encrypted, CADI ecosystem | ARM-only ISA; no Andes IP; per-core not full cluster | $100K-1M/yr |
127	| Imperas (now Synopsys) | Synopsys | RISC-V leader; DPI-to-RTL | functional ISS + RTL bridge, not true hybrid; expensive | $200K-2M/yr |
128	| Wind River Simics + Hindsight | Wind River | full-system; large install base | not cycle-exact; weak RISC-V perf modeling | $50K-500K/yr |
129	| **Andes HybridSim** | **Andes** | **first-class Andes IP, $0 cycle-side capex, bundled kanata** | **alpha today; Andes ISA only** | **$K-M/yr** |
130	
131	Tier 1 (ZeBu/Palladium/Veloce) is explicitly not our competitive
132	target. They serve customers who already have $M+ FPGA capex.
133	
134	Tier 3 (gem5, Spike+DPI) is not our competitive target either.
135	Open-source pulls revenue to zero; we ship Andes IP correlation as
136	a paid product.
137	
138	### 5.2 The wedge
139	
140	Three things competitors do not deliver together:
141	
142	1. **First-class Andes IP modeling** - vendor CSRs, ACE, AndeStar V5,
143	   Andes platform (AE350-class) out of the box. ARM and Imperas
144	   require customer integration work; Wind River is functional-only.
145	2. **Zero FPGA capex** - runs on a Linux workstation. ZeBu/Palladium
146	   need a $M+ board.
147	3. **Bundled kanata + handoff orchestrator** - competitors
148	   sell these as separate add-ons or do not ship them at all.
149	
150	### 5.3 Honest losses
151	
152	- vsim cycle-side speed (5-50 KHz) is 1000-10000x slower than ZeBu
153	  emulator (10-100 MHz). For ROIs longer than ~1B cycles, ZeBu wins.
154	  Mitigation: keep the cycle-engine ROI small; multi-instance parallel
155	  measurement.
156	- ISA coverage is RISC-V Andes-only. ARM Cycle Models cover ARM
157	  ecosystem; Imperas covers broad RISC-V. Mitigation: deepen Andes
158	  IP support to make depth beat breadth.
159	- Maturity: ARM Cycle Models are 10+ years productized. Our v1.0
160	  is a fresh product. Mitigation: design-partner program before
161	  general availability.
162	
163	---
164	
165	## 6. Business Model
166	
167	### 6.1 Pricing structure
168	
169	Three SKUs:
170	
171	| SKU | Audience | Includes | Price guidance |
172	|---|---|---|---|
173	| **HybridSim Workstation** | per-seat developer | full feature set, 1 named seat | $40K-80K/yr |
174	| **HybridSim Project** | per-project team | floating license pool (5-25 seats) | $200K-1M/yr |
175	| **HybridSim Academic** | universities, labs | feature-limited (no kanata export) | $5K-15K/yr |
176	
177	Add-ons (post-v1.0):
178	- Linux/SMP support pack (multi-hart, S/U-mode beyond v1.0 envelope)
179	- Custom Andes IP variant support (one-off NRE)
180	- Premium SLA (24h response, dedicated FAE)
181	
182	### 6.2 License enforcement
183	
184	- Network license daemon (FlexLM-class) per industry norm
185	- Node-locked option for air-gapped customers (HSM-bound)
186	- Floating pool with checkout / checkin
187	- Per-feature flags (kanata, vendor CSR pack)
188	- License expiry triggers graceful shutdown with checkpoint export
189	
190	### 6.3 Delivery channels
191	
192	- Direct (Andes sales) for top-50 accounts
193	- Distributor / reseller for long tail (e.g. through Andes regional
194	  partners in Japan, EU, US)
195	- Evaluation: 30-day full-feature trial under EULA, node-locked
196	
197	---
198	
199	## 7. Market Requirements
200	
201	Numbered MRs for traceability into FRS.md. Each MR has a status
202	relative to v1.0 ship.
203	
204	### MR-A - Cycle-exact ROI measurement on customer workloads
205	
206	Customer provides their own ELF (closed source). HybridSim
207	fast-forwards in QEMU, switches to cycle engine at ROI, returns a
208	cycle figure correlated with RTL within an explicit error budget.
209	
210	- Acceptance: closed-source customer ELF round-trips; cycle figure
211	  agrees with fully-RTL baseline within 1% on the ROI window.
212	
213	### MR-B - Linux + userspace ROI
214	
215	Boot Linux, reach userspace hot loop, hand off to cycle engine,
216	measure, then drain.
217	
218	- Acceptance: at least 3 SPEC-class workloads under Linux userspace
219	  ship a cycle figure end-to-end.
220	
221	### MR-D - Closed-source RTL protection (encryption)
222	
223	Cycle engine is RTL-derived (via Verilator) but the shipped binary
224	must not allow recovery of Andes RTL or microarch internals.
225	
226	- Acceptance: third-party reverse-engineering audit confirms no
227	  RTL recoverable from shipped binary; license + IP officer sign-off.
228	
229	### MR-E - Andes vendor CSR and ACE parity
230	
231	All customer-visible Andes vendor CSRs and ACE coherence flows
232	round-trip across the handoff with bit-exact semantics.
233	
234	- Acceptance: vendor-CSR conformance test suite passes 100%; ACE
235	  coherence regression passes on multi-hart workloads.
236	
237	### MR-F - Pipeline trace export (kanata)
238	
239	Customer can record kanata-format pipeline traces for the cycle
240	window with output byte-identical to a fully-RTL baseline.
241	
242	- Acceptance: kanata diff against fully-RTL baseline is empty for
243	  the cycle window.
244	
245	### MR-G - Iterative microarch tweak loop
246	
247	Architect changes a cycle-engine parameter (cache size, ROB depth),
248	rebuilds engine only, re-runs measurement against the same QEMU
249	checkpoint without re-running boot.
250	
251	- Acceptance: edit-rebuild-measure cycle under 5 minutes on a
252	  reference workload.
253	
254	### MR-H - Multi-hart support
255	
256	At least 4 harts in the cycle engine with coherent state transport
257	through ACE.
258	
259	- Acceptance: a 4-hart parallel kernel round-trips and produces a
260	  cycle figure within 1% of fully-RTL baseline.
261	
262	### MR-I - Determinism and reproducibility
263	
264	Identical inputs (ELF + config + seed) produce bit-identical cycle
265	counts and pipeline traces across runs and hosts.
266	
267	- Acceptance: a reproducibility test suite runs the same workload
268	  on 3 different hosts; all outputs bit-identical.
269	
270	### MR-J - CI / batch integration
271	
272	The product runs unattended in a CI environment. License daemon,
273	checkpointing, error reporting, and exit codes are CI-friendly.
274	
275	- Acceptance: a reference CI pipeline (GitLab / Jenkins) runs 20
276	  workloads in parallel, collects results, no manual intervention.
277	
278	### MR-K - First-class observability
279	
280	Every handoff, trigger, and state transport event is logged with
281	structured key=value format. Errors are actionable, not "internal
282	error".
283	
284	- Acceptance: a deliberate state-corruption injection produces a
285	  log message identifying the corrupted register and the handoff
286	  phase. No silent failures.
287	
288	---
289	
290	## 8. Go-to-Market & Delivery
291	
292	### 8.1 Design-partner phase (months 0-6 post-engineering complete)
293
